newsitem.title: ITALY: Olivetti fin position not worrying - Consob.
newsitem.headline: Olivetti fin position not worrying - Consob.

text.p: The financial position of Italy's information and technology group Olivetti is not worrying but further economic details on the firm will be needed by year-end, the head of Italy's stock market regulatory body said.

Enzo Berlanda told reporters that Olivetti directors had not talked to Consob of any possible capital increase at the loss making company but only of possible de-mergers and sales of some of its units.

"It is not the financial situation (at Olivetti ) which worries us, but we want the situation to be clear and that they say how things are going," Berlanda said before presenting a report on Olivetti to a parliamentary industry committee.
"Just as (Olivetti) presented data from the end of August, we will see to it that there are intermediary reports between here and the end of the year," he added.

Olivetti published its first half 1996 results in early September but on the very next day its director general in charge of finance and auditing Renzo Francesconi resigned after he cast doubts on the accuracy of its first half results.

After an initial inquiry by Consob, the stock market watchdog demanded further information, especially on its July and August period after the first-half had closed. Olivetti provided that information last month, revealing that its net group debt had nearly doubled in the two months following June.
